rich_summary: After completing his search and confirming Sita’s presence, Hanuman considers how best to further harm the titans of Lanka before returning to Rama. Deciding that the destruction of the city will complete his mission, he uses the flames on his tail to ignite the mansions of the demon nobles. Leaping from roof to roof with immense speed, he sets ablaze the palaces of many powerful rakshasas and finally Ravana’s own resplendent residence. The fire spreads across Lanka like a cosmic catastrophe, fanned by the wind, melting jewels and metals and sending the inhabitants into panic. Demons wonder if the blazing monkey is actually a god in disguise—Agni, Indra, or even Vishnu’s power. As the city burns, the heavens rejoice, praising Hanuman’s divine strength and heroic devastation.

highlight_spans.why: Hanuman’s inner resolve—he reflects on how best to complete his mission by afflicting the titans further.
The pivotal decision: after destroying the grove and slaying demons, Hanuman concludes that burning Lanka itself will finish the task.
The chapter heading marking the famous episode of Hanuman setting Lanka ablaze.

top_scenes.scene_text: Hanuman, his long tail wrapped in blazing fire, leaps across the golden rooftops of Lanka at night as flames spread from palace to palace.
The jeweled palace of Ravana ignites as Hanuman touches it with his burning tail, the wind fanning a colossal inferno across the demon city.
From a high rooftop, Hanuman watches the vast city of Lanka engulfed in fire, molten gold and gems flowing from collapsing towers while demons flee in terror.
